---
title: "Fetching the data"
---

No data file is in the package. The third-party originals (341 MB) belong to
the people who produced them, and the converted reference data (10 MB) is
derived from them. Both are in the gadopt object store and are served at
`https://data.gadopt.org/giamip/`. Every file is checked against the SHA-256
sum in `giamip/resources/manifest.json`, so a file that the package reads is
the file that the manifest describes.

## On first use

A reader asks for a file with `giamip.data.locate`, and every reader of the
package does this. For example, `BenchmarkResult.reference_path("B")` calls:

```python
from giamip import data
data.locate("martinec2018/martinec2018-B.nc", "converted")
```

`locate` looks in two places:

1. `data/<stage>/` of the checkout, when the package runs from one;
2. the download root: `$GIAMIP_DATA_ROOT` when it is set, else `data/` of
   the checkout, else `~/.cache/giamip`.

When neither has the file, `locate` downloads it into the download root,
checks its sum and, for an archive, unpacks it. A file is identified by its
sum, so it does not matter which of two identical copies is read.

`locate` never reads `XDG_CACHE_HOME`. On Gadi the Firedrake module points it
at storage that is deleted when the job ends, so a cache there would be empty
in every job.

## Where the files go

Under a root, an original is at `original/<key>`, for example
`original/giamip/ice-history.zip`. A converted file is at
`versions/<sha256>/<key>`, for example
`versions/104e8a…/martinec2018/martinec2018-B.nc`. The sum in the path gives
every version of a converted file its own place, so two versions of giamip
that share one cache never overwrite each other's files. In a checkout,
`data/versions/` is ignored by git, and the tracked files in
`data/converted/` are never overwritten.

Archives are unpacked into a directory named after the archive, with the
archive's single top-level directory removed when it has one, so
`giamip/ice-history.zip` gives
`giamip/ice-history/iceHistory-ICE-6G_D.nc`. A stamp file inside the target
records which archive it came from, so a second run neither extracts 317 MB
again nor disturbs anything you put there.

## When a file is wrong

A file in place whose sum is not the manifest's is handled by its kind:

- **A converted file in the checkout's `data/converted/`**: `locate` raises
  and names `scripts/build_manifest.py`. This is the state after a conversion
  and before the manifest is rebuilt.
- **A converted file under `versions/`**: the path names the sum, so the file
  is damaged. `locate` downloads it again.
- **An original**: `locate` raises and gives the command that replaces the
  file. It never replaces an original by itself. The GIAMIP inputs change
  under one name, and a file on disk can be the only copy of a previous
  version, which the store no longer has. `GiamipExperiment` and the GIAMIP
  readers take a `root` argument to read such a version on purpose.

## Many processes, and no network

The download and the unpack of one file run under a file lock
(`.<name>.lock`, beside the file). When the ranks of an MPI job start at
once, one downloads and the others wait and then read. On Gadi, `/g/data`
and `/scratch` are mounted with `localflock`, so the lock excludes only the
processes on one node.

A download that fails raises `DataUnavailable`. Its message gives the URL,
the reason, and the command that fills a directory on a machine with network
access. The failure is recorded in `.<name>.failed` for 60 s, so the other
processes of the job raise at once and do not each wait for the 30 s timeout.
The command below ignores that record.

::: {.callout-important}
## Gadi

Compute nodes have no network. Fill a directory on a login node once, and
point the job at it:

```bash
# on a login node
GIAMIP_DATA_ROOT=/g/data/<project>/giamip \
    python -m giamip.data --stage converted --collection benchmarks
# in the job script
export GIAMIP_DATA_ROOT=/g/data/<project>/giamip
```

Add `--collection giamip` (with the default stage, `original`) for the
GIAMIP inputs, 317 MB. The Firedrake module must have giamip installed with
its dependencies h5netcdf and `packaging`; h5py, numpy and scipy are in the
module already.
:::

## The command line

```bash
python -m giamip.data                         # both benchmarks, the originals
python -m giamip.data --stage converted       # the converted reference data
python -m giamip.data --collection giamip     # the GIAMIP inputs, 317 MB
python -m giamip.data --all                   # every collection
python -m giamip.data --list                  # what exists, and what is local
python -m giamip.data --verify --all          # check the sums, download nothing
python -m giamip.data --dest DIR              # fill DIR, not the download root
```

`--collection` takes `spada2011`, `martinec2018` or `giamip`, and `benchmarks`
as an alias for the first two. `--stage` takes `original`, the default, for an
untouched third-party file, or `converted` for a file this project derived
from one. In a checkout filled by default, a tracked converted file that
matches the manifest is reported `ok` and not downloaded again.

`--verify` reports a file that is missing or whose sum has changed, and exits
non-zero. Run it after you copy a tree between machines.

::: {.callout-note}
## Only granted files are downloaded

`locate` and `python -m giamip.data` refuse to download a file whose
`permission` is not `granted`. Today every file in the manifest is granted and
public. A file added later starts as `requested` or `not_asked`. Until its
supplier agrees, obtain the file from the supplier and put it in
`data/original/` by hand, in the layout that the manifest describes.
[The manifest](manifest.qmd) records the permission state of every file.
:::
